learning_objective: 🎯 Move beyond hard news! Learn how to weave facts, human emotions, and storytelling techniques to write captivating feature articles for newspapers and magazines.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: News tells you *what* happened yesterday (facts, urgency). A feature tells you *how* and *why* it happened, focusing on the people involved, emotions, and background context. Features are 'timeless'.

Unlike news that uses an 'inverted pyramid' (most important facts first), features use a narrative hook. You can start with a descriptive scene, a shocking quote, or a compelling short anecdote to grab the reader.
The best features put a human face on a large issue. Instead of writing about 'Poverty Statistics', a feature writes about the daily life of one specific family struggling to buy groceries.
Features rely heavily on interviewing people. Direct quotes breathe life into the text. Good feature writers don't just quote facts; they quote opinions, emotions, and unique ways of speaking.

A feature doesn't just fade out; it ends with a 'kicker'. This is a memorable closing thought, a full-circle reference back to the opening lead, or a powerful final quote that leaves a lasting impact.

fun_activity.title: 👵 The Grandparent Profile
fun_activity.instructions: Sit down with an older relative and interview them for 10 minutes about their teenage years. Write a 200-word 'mini-feature' focusing entirely on one specific, funny, or emotional memory they shared.

exam_tips: 📌 Always start a feature writing task with a catchy title and an engaging introductory paragraph (the hook).
📌 Blend facts with description. Don't just list data; weave the statistics naturally into the story you are telling.
📌 Keep the tone appropriate to the subject. A feature on a local festival should be lively, while a feature on climate change should be reflective and serious.
quick_recap: ⭐ Feature articles read more like short stories than traditional hard news reports.
⭐ Anecdotes are the secret weapon of feature writing—they make abstract topics relatable.
⭐ The ending of a feature (the kicker) should resonate emotionally with the reader.
